title: End of the Covered Season and Closure of a Protection Plan Record
content:
A Pass and Trip Protection plan covers one season and ends with it.

1. On the season's last day cover stops, whether the plan was in force, stopped for non-payment or carrying a
   settled claim, and the record is marked expired.
2. A settled claim is closed off by returning the plan to force with the benefit reduced by what was paid, so
   a plan with an allowance of more than one claim may be claimed on again in the same season up to the
   benefit left.
3. Expiry does not cancel what is still owed: premium instalments still to fall are presented after expiry
   exactly as before.
4. A plan record is closed only when no premium is left to collect and no allowed claim is left to pay, which
   is answered from the collective's own plan record — the premium still to be collected standing on it and
   how any claim on it was decided — before the record is closed.
5. Closing is the last write on the record and nothing is added to it afterwards.
6. A household who wants cover for the next season takes a fresh plan over the holding they open for that
   season.

**Illustrations (hypothetical).** A plan with an allowance of 2 claims in the season, one claim settled and
paid in January: the plan returns to force with the benefit reduced by what was paid, and a second claim may
be made in the same season up to the benefit left. A plan standing at the season's end with premium still to
be collected is marked expired, its remaining instalments are still presented, and its record is not closed
until nothing is left to collect and no allowed claim is left to pay.
